correctness.rationale: With the stated energy ordering, the aged coherence is c exp(iΩa). Integrating it over an equilibrium renewal interval gives χ=(E exp(iX)-1)/(im), X=ΩT>0 with E X=m. Purity is P0+2|c|²|χ|²; this is purity of the averaged state, not average trajectory purity. The chord function 2|sin(X/2)| is bounded by its concave majorant (2 sin(X/2) up to π; 2 thereafter). For m<π a supporting tangent contacts that majorant only at m, and at m≥π unit-circle equality forces odd multiples of π, with m=π forcing a point mass. All means ≥π can be represented by adjacent odd multiples. At the lower edge E(1-cos X)=0 is equivalent to full-turn support, which is feasible exactly for m≥2π because zero is excluded. Below 2π, the epsilon/2π law shows the limiting infimum. Convex mixtures at fixed mean and continuity give the entire displayed interval. Independent numerical age integrals at m/π=1/2, 1, 2, 3 confirmed the upper endpoints and exact full-turn cancellation to numerical precision (private replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py, qubit_check). No uploaded checker executed; finite checks alone do not prove the theorem.

Wald et al. work with discrete-time reset gates and age ensembles; Rose et al. impose Poisson resetting. Neither clock restriction covers arbitrary positive continuous waiting lengths.

value.rationale: The physically prescribed mean imposes an attainable coherence budget, not just an age-average expression. The upper extremizer switches from a unique regular schedule to all mean-matched odd-half-turn laws; combining this with the known full-turn cancellation constraint decides exactly which purities a stationary clock can produce. The comparison includes broad and deterministic clocks and does not confuse time-phase convergence with the stationary ensemble.
